In the very middle, a metal ring C is suspended with an insulating thread. The ring and the wire are in the same vertical plane. During the process in which the current I increases, which of the following statements is correct ( )

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a long wire is bent into a shape with the upper part horizontal and the left and right sides vertical; the lower left end is marked “+”, and the lower right end is marked “-”. Beside the left vertical wire, the current I is marked upward, so the current goes upward along the left vertical segment, through the upper horizontal segment, and then downward along the right vertical segment. The metal ring C is suspended on the central insulating thread, located at the exact middle position between the left and right vertical wires, and is in the same vertical plane as the wire. Reasoning: When the current I increases, the magnetic flux passing through the metal ring C changes accordingly, so an induced current is produced in the ring, and the direction of the induced current always opposes the increase of magnetic flux. When analyzing the force on the ring, since the metal ring is on the symmetrical center line of the two left and right vertical wires, the horizontal magnetic forces produced by the two left and right vertical wires on the metal ring are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so the horizontal resultant force is zero, and no resultant torque causing the ring to deflect will be produced either. In the vertical direction there may be the influence of magnetic force, but the tension of the insulating thread suspending the ring can adjust accordingly to balance gravity and the vertical magnetic force. Therefore the ring will not move to the left or to the right, nor will it rotate, and it can still maintain rest.
